questions.text:
The relation scheme given below is used to store information about the employees of a company, where empId is the key and deptId indicates the department to which the employee is assigned. Each employee is assigned to exactly one department.

[latex]\textsf{emp($\underline{\textsf{empId}}$, name, gender, salary, deptId)}[/latex]

Consider the following SQL query:
 select deptId, count(*)
from emp
where gender = "female" and salary > (select avg(salary)from emp)
group by deptId;
The above query gives, for each department in the company, the number of female employees whose salary is greater than the average salary of
questions.solution:
The subquery (select avg(salary) from emp) has no condition and is not correlated, so it is the average salary of all employees in the company.

Answer: employees in the company

questions.text:
Let S be the following schedule of operations of three transactions [latex]T_1, T_2 \text{ and }T_3[/latex] in a relational database system:

[latex]R_2(Y), R_1(X), R_3(Z), R_1(Y)W_1(X), R_2(Z), W_2(Y), R_3(X), W_3(Z)[/latex]

Consider the statements P and Q below:

P: S is conflict-serializable.
Q: If [latex]T_3[/latex] commits before [latex]T_1[/latex] finishes, then S is recoverable.

Which one of the following choices is correct?
questions.solution:
Conflicts:
- [latex]R_1(Y)[/latex] before [latex]W_2(Y)[/latex]: T1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T2
- [latex]W_1(X)[/latex] before [latex]R_3(X)[/latex]: T1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3
- [latex]R_2(Z)[/latex] before [latex]W_3(Z)[/latex]: T2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3
No cycle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] conflict serializable (T1, T2, T3). P is true.

T3 reads X written by T1. If T3 commits before T1, and T1 later aborts, T3 cannot be undone [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not recoverable. Q is false.

Answer: P is true and Q is false

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Both P and Q are true
P is true and Q is false
P is false and Q is true
Both P and Q are false

questions.text: A bag has [latex]r[/latex] red balls and [latex]b[/latex] black balls. All balls are identical except for their colours. In a trial, a ball is randomly drawn from the bag, its colour is noted and the ball is placed back into the bag along with another ball of the same colour. Note that the number of balls in the bag will increase by one, after the trial. A sequence of four such trials is conducted. Which one of the following choices gives the probability of drawing a red ball in the fourth trial?
questions.solution:
This is Polya's urn. By symmetry, every draw has the same chance of being red as the first draw.

Check for the 2nd draw: [latex]\frac{r}{r+b}\cdot\frac{r+1}{r+b+1}+\frac{b}{r+b}\cdot\frac{r}{r+b+1}=\frac{r(r+b+1)}{(r+b)(r+b+1)}=\frac{r}{r+b}[/latex]. The same holds for the 4th.

Answer: [latex]\frac{r}{r+b}[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: Consider the cyclic redundancy check (CRC) based error detecting scheme having the generator polynomial [latex]X^3+X+1[/latex]. Suppose the message [latex]m_4m_3m_2m_1m_0=11000[/latex] is to be transmitted. Check bits [latex]c_2c_1c_0[/latex] are appended at the end of the message by the transmitter using the above CRC scheme. The transmitted bit string is denoted by [latex]m_4m_3m_2m_1m_0c_2c_1c_0[/latex]. The value of the checkbit sequence [latex]c_2c_1c_0[/latex] is
questions.solution:
Generator [latex]x^3+x+1[/latex] = 1011. Append 3 zeros: 11000000, then divide (XOR):
- 1100 [latex]\oplus[/latex] 1011 = 0111 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] bring 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1110
- 1110 [latex]\oplus[/latex] 1011 = 0101 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] bring 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1010
- 1010 [latex]\oplus[/latex] 1011 = 0001 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] bring 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0010 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] bring 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0100

Remainder = 100

Answer: 100

The list has 4 nodes (values 0, 1, 2, 3). The last node's next is never set; malloc does not initialize it.

In the last loop pass (index = 3), head moves to the 4th node and then to its next (garbage), and the second printf dereferences that pointer [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undefined behaviour / possible crash.

(A missing return in main is allowed in C.)

Answer: It dereferences an uninitialized pointer that may result in a run-time error
